actions.label: Approve per-app FancyZones history design
actions.note: Approve a full implementation design that separates app-zone history for shared-host apps such as Edge PWAs.

issue_context.summary: FancyZones remembers last zones by executable path, so every Edge PWA hosted by msedge.exe is treated as the same app when zones are restored.
known_information: The issue describes multiple PWAs sharing msedge.exe or msedge_proxy.exe and reopening in the wrong prior zone.
AppZoneHistory::SetAppLastZones stores history under the string returned by get_process_path_waiting_uwp(window).
AppZoneHistory::GetZoneHistory later retrieves by that same app-path key.
The serialized history schema in AppZoneHistory.h currently only defines `app-path` as the app identity field.
Workspaces already contains public code for retrieving a window AppUserModelId through SHGetPropertyStoreForWindow / PKEY_AppUserModel_ID.
inferences: Any hosted-app model where multiple logical apps share one executable path can collide in FancyZones zone history, not just Edge PWAs.
AUMID or a similar per-window app identity is the natural discriminator because the current repo already uses it elsewhere for launch/restore logic.
issue_context.analysis: This is good design work for the batch. The failure mechanism is straightforward, the affected persistence layer is localized, and the repo already has one app-identity implementation pattern that FancyZones can reuse or extract.
initial_investigation: Reviewed src/modules/fancyzones/FancyZonesLib/FancyZonesData/AppZoneHistory.cpp and confirmed process-path-only storage and lookup.
Reviewed AppZoneHistory.h and confirmed the persisted schema only exposes `app-path` today.
Reviewed src/modules/Workspaces/WorkspacesLib/WindowUtils.cpp and confirmed the repo already reads AppUserModelId from a window/property store.
Reviewed AppZoneHistory unit tests and identified the existing parse/lookup coverage that should be extended for richer app identities.

judgment.rationale: FancyZones currently keys last-zone history by process path, so distinct Edge PWAs that all run under msedge.exe collide into one shared zone-history bucket.
evidence: AppZoneHistory.cpp calls get_process_path_waiting_uwp(window) and uses that returned path as the map key for m_history.
GetZoneHistory looks up the same app-path key later when restoring zones.
The issue explains that Edge PWAs share msedge.exe/msedge_proxy.exe while remaining logically distinct apps, which matches the current storage key collision.
The repo already contains AppUserModelId helpers in Workspaces/WorkspacesLib/WindowUtils.cpp, showing there is an existing code pattern for a window-specific app identity.
judgment.recommended_action: Approve a design that augments FancyZones app-zone history with a window/app identity stronger than raw process path for Edge PWAs and similar shared-host apps.

fix_assessment.rationale: There is no linked fix attempt yet, but the ownership path, persisted data format, and likely identity source are all narrow and code-backed.

proposed_fixes.title: Key FancyZones app-zone history by executable path plus app identity
proposed_fixes.root_cause: FancyZones persists and restores zone history using only the process path returned by get_process_path_waiting_uwp(window). For Edge PWAs, many distinct apps share the same host executable, so the last opened PWA overwrites the saved zone history for the others.
plan: Add a stable app-identity helper that can read an AppUserModelId from the target window and combine it with the executable path when available.
Teach AppZoneHistory to serialize and deserialize that richer identity while still reading legacy app-path-only entries.
Prefer the richer identity for restore and update paths so different PWAs hosted by msedge.exe stop colliding.
verification: Launch two different Edge PWAs, zone them separately, close both, and verify each relaunches to its own last zone instead of the most recently zoned PWA location.
Confirm ordinary single-identity desktop apps still reuse their existing app-path history entries.

confidence.rationale: The collision is directly explained by the current map key and the issue supplies the exact shared-host scenario that breaks it.

design.root_cause: FancyZones persists app-zone history under a single `app-path` string produced from the target window’s process path. Distinct Edge PWAs all resolve to the same host executable (`msedge.exe`/`msedge_proxy.exe`), so one PWA overwrites the saved zone history for another and later restores read the wrong entry.
evidence: src/modules/fancyzones/FancyZonesLib/FancyZonesData/AppZoneHistory.cpp:452-490 looks up the same appPath key in GetZoneHistory when restoring zone placement.
src/modules/fancyzones/FancyZonesLib/FancyZonesData/AppZoneHistory.h only persists one app identity field today: `app-path`.
src/modules/Workspaces/WorkspacesLib/WindowUtils.cpp already contains a working `GetAUMIDFromWindow` implementation using SHGetPropertyStoreForWindow and PKEY_AppUserModel_ID.
Issue 50304 provides the precise shared-host scenario: multiple Edge PWAs all hosted by msedge.exe but expected to reopen in distinct zones.

affected_files.purpose: Defines the persisted app-zone history schema and the in-memory map contract.
Loads, saves, sets, removes, and looks up app-zone history entries.
Current shared helper surface for deriving a window process path; likely place to add a richer app identity helper if FancyZones should not depend on Workspaces.
Existing repository implementation pattern for obtaining an AppUserModelId from a window.
Existing serialization and lookup tests that should cover richer app identities and legacy fallback.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: FancyZones can cheaply derive only a process path for a window, so shared-host applications collapse into one identity.
implementation_steps.change: Add a helper that returns a richer app identity: the process path plus an optional AppUserModelId read from the window/property store or process package metadata when present.
edge_cases: Return an empty AUMID for classic Win32 apps so their identity remains process-path-only.
Do not block indefinitely on packaged/UWP windows; preserve the existing retry behavior from get_process_path_waiting_uwp.
tests: Add a helper-level test or mock coverage that verifies an empty AUMID falls back to process-path-only identity.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: The persisted schema and map key expose only `app-path`, so different logical apps sharing one executable cannot be separated.
implementation_steps.change: Extend the schema with an optional app-identity field (for example `app-user-model-id`) and define a normalized composite in-memory key that uses process path plus AUMID when available.
edge_cases: Keep backward compatibility with existing app-zone-history.json files that only contain app-path.
Avoid changing unrelated consumers that only need the persisted file path name.
tests: Add parse coverage for both legacy app-path-only entries and new path-plus-AUMID entries.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: Set, lookup, and removal all key into m_history using only processPath.
implementation_steps.change: Build a normalized key from `{processPath, appUserModelId}` when available, save both fields to JSON, and make lookup prefer the richer key while still falling back to legacy process-path entries if no richer entry exists.
edge_cases: If an old history entry exists for msedge.exe without AUMID, do not lose it abruptly; migrate on next write after a richer identity is observed.
If SHGetPropertyStoreForWindow does not return an AUMID for a particular host window, fall back cleanly to processPath so classic apps remain unchanged.
tests: Add a regression test that writes two app-zone-history entries with the same process path but different AUMIDs and verifies they restore separately.
Add a fallback test proving a legacy process-path-only entry is still returned when no richer identity exists.

verify: Build FancyZones and run the existing AppZoneHistory unit tests after adding path-plus-AUMID coverage.
Install two Edge PWAs, assign each to a different zone, close them, and relaunch them individually to verify each one reopens in its own saved zone.
Retest a normal Win32 app and a UWP-hosted app to confirm existing path-only restore behavior still works when no AUMID is available.
risks: Changing the persisted history key format can strand or misread existing app-zone-history.json entries if legacy fallback is not preserved.
Window AUMID discovery can fail for some host windows; the implementation must degrade to process-path behavior instead of dropping history.
Using a richer identity only for some apps can create duplicates if normalization between old and new keys is inconsistent.
alternatives: Keep keying only by process path and special-case msedge.exe with command-line parsing; rejected because it would be brittle and still miss other shared-host app models.
Key by window title; rejected because titles are user-visible, localized, and unstable across sessions.
